Moraine Mayor's court is located in the County of Montgomery, Ohio. It has jurisdiction over criminal, felony or misdemeanors matters and traffic and vehicle offenses. The cases are handled by the mayor, and most traffic cases are prosecuted by the Montgomery County District Attorney. This court has limited jurisdiction and is not a court of records. Some rules are made by this court that should be followed by every person in the courthouse. The court session was held every Wednesday.

Which type of misdemeanor cases are handled by this court?

Moraine Mayor's court handles misdemeanor cases that involve the following:

  • Publicly Gambling
  • Chaotic Conduct
  • Trespass of Criminal
  • Violation in curfew

This court handles all minor misdemeanor cases. This court does not take domestic violence and protective order cases.

How to search for court records?

Moraine Mayor's court records search can be done online as; well all the records are available in the clerk's office and county clerk's office, so that anyone can search from these offices. All the case information and trails are recorded and maintained by the county and clerk's office. They can be searched online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by name and city/state
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Sometimes, case information records are unavailable online because it is confidential according to the law, like criminal cases etc. These types of information are only available at the county court or county clerk's office. They can be obtained by filing and sending a record request form. Fill in all the required information on the form. Send the fees for the copies of the record. After receiving the form, the court will respond with whether to provide this information. For more information about the public records, call or mail the court.

see also Lehigh County Courthouse

What is the procedure for sending a public record request?

Moraine Mayor's court public record request had some procedures or steps. These steps are:

  • Fill out all the information in the form of a public record request. Give a clear reason why you want these records.
  • Submit it to the city department or clerk's office.
  • After the department receives your form, the clerk will send them to the department of law. The law department will review your form and respond to whether or not the records should be given. Some records are not disclosed according to the law of Ohio.
  • If your request is accepted, you must send some fees for the copies of the records.

How to make payments?

Moraine Mayor's Court payments for tickets and fines can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter. Take your ticket when you are coming for payment. 2.99% processing and other charges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online

The Online Payment can be made using the Ohio Online Payment Portal https://www.mccountycourts.org/onlinepayment/. Enter the case or ticket number. Select the payment method. The service fees will be applied in this case.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address. The address is 4200 Dryden Rd, Moraine, OH 45439, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write

your citation when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

What are the penalties of this court?

Moraine Mayor's Court penalties will be settled in court. These penalties are categories that are given below:

  • First-Degree Misdemeanors:

In this case, the punishment is a fine of up to $1000 and 180 days in jail.

  • Second-Degree Misdemeanors:

In this case, the punishment is a fine of up to $750 and 90 days in jail.

  • Third-Degree Misdemeanors:

In this case, the punishment is a fine of up to 500 and 60 days in jail.

  • Fourth-Degree Misdemeanors:

In this case, the punishment is a fine of up to $250 and 30 days in jail.

  • Small/Minor Misdemeanors:

In this case, a fine of up to $150 is the punishment. No jail in this punishment.

How can I send a plea by mail?

Moraine Mayor's Court plea can only be written if you received a traffic infraction, vehicle, speeding, or parking ticket. Write a plea and send it before the citation date noted on your ticket. Download the plea form, choose the plea you want, write your name and email address date, and sign your signature. Two types of plea can be written and mailed to the court that are:

see also Hardy County Magistrate Clerk

Plea of Guilty

Choose a guilty plea if you admit you violated the law or committed a crime. The court will review your application and respond with the fine amount or, in severe cases, with a court date. You can request to attend the traffic school in this plea.

Plea of Not Guilty

If you do not accept your offense and deny all the violations against you, then choose the plea of not guilty. The court will review your application and send you a schedule for your court appearance, and you have to appear on time. Firstly a trial date is given to you, and you must appear with all the proof in your defense. Hire an attorney in this case. You cannot request traffic school in this case.

How can I attend the traffic school?

Moraine Mayor's Court traffic schools are for that person who violated traffic or vehicle rules or was involved in a speeding case, and the person had written a plea of guilty. Traffic school can be attended by submitting your information like first and last name online. The court will review your case and respond if you are eligible for the school. You had to pay the fees for the school course if the court accepted you.

FAQ:

When will the trial session for this court be held?

Moraine Mayor's Court trial session will be held every Wednesday at 2:15 pm.

What are the rules of this court?

Moraine Mayor's Court rules are:

  • No weapons are allowed in this court
  • Appropriate, neat and proper attire should be worn by every person that visits the court.
  • Bad and offensive language is not allowed during court sessions.
  • No drinking or eating items are permitted.
  • Cell phones should be switched off during the court session.
How many fines a person had to pay if their phone starts ringing during the court session?

The court takes the phone, and after paying $25, the court returns the phone.
